steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 9x13-inch pan.
Stir cocoa and baking soda together in a large bowl.
Mix in 1/3 cup oil and boiling water until combined and thick.
Stir in sugar, remaining 1/3 cup oil, and eggs. Mix in flour, vanilla, and salt until flour is just absorbed.
Spread evenly into the prepared pan.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean, 35 to 40 minutes. Let cool completely before cutting into 24 squares.

raw_recipe.headline: Fudgy Brownies
raw_recipe.description: Try this easy fudgy brownie recipe for sweet, chewy treats for any occasion made with simple ingredients you probably already have in your pantry.

review.reviewBody: These brownies turned out PERFECT! Instead of baking them in a 9x13 pan, I made them in an 8x11 so that they were just a little thicker and I followed someone else's suggestion for adding the second 1/3 cup of oil BEFORE the eggs and sugar. I also added about half a bag of semi-sweet chocolate chips (I never make brownies without them!) and Oh My Goodness! These were the best home made brownies I've ever made! I've already put the recipe in my card box. :o)

This is my go to base recipe for Brownies. I substitute 1/3 of a cup of pure melted cocoa butter + 1/3 of a cup of oil instead of 2/3 of a cup of just oil. The cocoa butter might fool some into believing that these dairy free brownies were made with real butter. I mix a 1/2 cup or so of chopped walnuts into the batter. As in my mind, brownies must have walnuts! I also mix a 1/2 cup of mini chocolate chips into the batter to provide some richness. The addition of cocoa butter requires more chocolate. I like my brownies soft, so I only cook them 25 mins. Enjoy!

In most baked goods, like muffins & brownies, I halve the oil and sub with no-sugar added applesauce. I decreased the sugar from 2 cups to 1.5 cups without issue. After watching America's Test Kitchen, I added 1 t of espresso powder which intensifies the chocolate flavor. 1c chopped walnuts adds a nice texture and improves nutrition profile. Next time I make these, I'll add choc or mint choc chips.

The brownies came out yummy. I used avocado oil. I also baked them in a shallow pan in the Insta Vortex Oven at 325 degrees for 7 minutes. I made 20 mini brownies and saved the other half of the batter to make later. Easy recipe. Thank you for sharing!

I made some changes to this recipe so I don't feel I can fairly give it a 5 star rating, but in all fairness, I think it deserves 5 stars! My husband is diabetic so I was looking for a sugar free brownie recipe. I saw this recipe & read some of the reviews. I thought I would give this one a try BUT replace the sugar with Splenda! Both my husband & my son (non diabetic but feels sugar free is best for him & his 2 yr old daughter) after their taste test, raised their eyebrow & said "Wow, these are good!" When I told them they are sugar free, they both were seriously pleased!!
My only comment on the original recipe is I baked mine in a smaller pan (7" x 10") because the recipe clearly does not make enough for a 9" x 12" pan. I also baked for 30minutes and brownies should be baked for 28 min to get a nice constancy, in my opinion. This recipe is very easy and the chocolate flavor is perfect for us, not overpowering. Yes, I will definitely make this again!!! Thank you for sharing your recipe!!!

Delicious! Perfect fudgy texture. They have a bit of a crackle top that I just love and they are not too sweet. Served with Dairy Queen soft serve and warm fudge sauce. Took great care not to overmix so I could ensure that I got that fudgy feel. Made some slight adjustments: I too added all the oil at once. I'm curious to know why its separated. Also added the vanilla in with the egg. I generally do that anyway as I feel it prob disperses it better. Not sure how true that might be, but I've never had anything turn out poorly as a result. Also baked for only 30 minutes. I might even reduce that a tad more next time. Of note was the strange sound it made for a few minutes after I removed it from the oven. Sort of like it was boiling.

I cut down the sugar by 1/4 cup and added mini chocolate chips at the end. Also if you cut down the baking time by 5-10 minutes (depending on your oven), it will turn out a lot more fudgy. 
I’ve been making this recipe for years now and it’s still my go-to brownie recipe!

This is definitely my favorite brownie recipe! I usually add the salt and sugar before the boiling water first so they will dissolve into the batter better. I never everrr use anything to measure but the 1/3 cup, 1/2 cup, etc.. to make this recipe since it is so easy to add too much flour or not enough liquid. They are PERFECT with 1-3 cups of semi-sweet, dark, and white chocolate chips! (I usually just pour in partial bags) They are so rich and yummy! But do make sure to let the batter cool before adding your eggs (large eggs are best) and don't over mix the batter or it will become more cakey. Try it!

Don't know who taught you to cook, but evidently someone who doesn't know to blend oil and eggs and sugar first.(Called creaming together) Also the use of 2/3cup of oil is unneeded when you already have 1/2 boiling water. If you need more liquid add more water, not more oil. Your dry ingredients should be added last and would keep you from needing the additional oil.
I followed this recipe as is, only adding 1/2 cup of chocolate chips just before incorporating flour. I used 9x9 pan to make them super thick and just baked a tad longer than this recipe states.

They were chewy, that was a good thing. They were lacking in the chocolate flavor though, didn't taste it at all actually. I would suggest at least a full cup of cocoa and 1 tsp and a half of vanilla. This recipe is laid out to be able to more before adding the flour though so taste as you go.
They were delishous and a family favorite 😁
we used baking powder insted of soda also baked it for to long

I've used this method for years! Found it in a magazine ad from Hershey! It's amazing how the hot water thickens the batter when you stir it in, then add the rest of the oil and other ingredients. Don't doubt it till you try it.
It was alright for the most part

This was a unique way to assemble the batter. It felt like I was missing steps when I added just flour, because I am used to mixing all the dry together first, but this method worked. The brownies are okay, but are a bit dry and could use richer chocolate flavor. I baked these the minimum time stated. My usual recipe is fudgier and richer but it also uses butter and more cocoa, and I am always up for trying a new recipe and this sounded good. It was fine, but not quite what I was expecting. I think if I had pulled them from the oven sooner they would be fudgier and moister, but still not as chocolatey as I like. This was better than any boxed mix.
It's a bit on the sweeter side but these were AMAZING
